:::{#exm-indset-to-clique}
#### From independent sets to cliques

A set $S$ of vertices is independent in $G$
exactly when no two vertices of $S$ are joined in $G$,
which is exactly when every two vertices of $S$ are joined
in the [complement](#def-complement-graph) $\bar G$,
that is, when $S$ is a [clique](#def-clique) in $\bar G$.
So the function $f(G, k) = (\bar G, k)$ satisfies

$$
(G, k) \in \text{INDSET}
\quad \text{if and only if} \quad
(\bar G, k) \in \text{CLIQUE}.
$$

With $m$ vertices, computing $\bar G$
flips the $m(m - 1)$ off-diagonal entries of the adjacency matrix,
which takes $O(m^2)$ steps.
So INDSET $\le_p$ CLIQUE (@def-reduction).
CLIQUE is in NP, since a clique is its own certificate, as in
[the INDSET example](p-and-np.qmd#exm-indset-in-np).
INDSET is NP-complete (@thm-indset-np-complete),
so CLIQUE is NP-complete too, by @thm-np-complete-by-reduction.

:::
